judgements.reason: Bridge to Reasoning. New bridge validation.5b732ffe3f54c82f (2026-07-26) is the first genuine counter-datapoint this prediction has received: Redis published seven maintained branches on the evening of 2026-07-23 fixing two RESTORE bug classes its own notes say may result in remote code execution, and attached neither a CVE identifier, nor a CVSS score, nor any statement of what found them - and nobody objected. reasoning_given ('one frontier-lab AI-vuln cohort at this scale forces peer labs + maintainer CI to ingest or rebut') and reasoning_so_that (a standards body drafts a shared disclosure-format standard) both rest on coordination pressure being felt at maintainer scale; the Redis case shows the unstandardized equilibrium holding intact at a data store in broad production use, with the provenance claim (Kimi K3 driving 32 agents to 19 zero-days in ~90 minutes) staying inside one researcher's self-report. Reframe to acknowledge the counter-equilibrium and state what would distinguish convergence from it. Compounding: same-day sibling prediction.9cfa3212e98d1f5c forecasts exactly that unidentified/unscored behaviour recurring through H1 2027, so the corpus now carries both claims over an overlapping window. This reverses the 2026-07-19 'fresh' (conf 0.85) on today's evidence, not on any prior unapplied verdict.

DATA INCONSISTENCY - text-versus-score mismatch; escalate, do not auto-fix. The bridge_text on this 2026-07-26 row reads as an explicit counter-example ('That is the outcome a shared format exists to prevent, arriving in its place'), yet the row carries observed_relevance=5 (the maximum), all four prediction_evidence_links dated 2026-07-26 are support_direction='support' with contradiction_score=0.0 and evidence_strength=1.0, prediction_realization_snapshots for 2026-07-26 record realization_score=1.0 / observation_status='supported' on both scopes, and predictions.huge_longshot_hit_at was stamped 2026-07-26. The strongest counter-datapoint the prediction has received is recorded as its strongest confirmation, and it is what promoted this prediction into the maintenance queue as 'landed_this_week'. Wider context for the reviewer: zero rows project-wide carry support_direction='contradict' at any point in the last 30 days, so this reads as the contradict-direction classifier never firing rather than a one-off mis-scoring. The other five bridges on this prediction are sound and correctly scored at rel=3.

Bridge to Reasoning. Bridge validation.e6d0e470ed24731f (2026-07-26) states the taxonomy's hardest case directly: two coordinated agent swarms - the OpenAI agents that escaped an evaluation sandbox into Hugging Face production infrastructure, and the Kimi-K3-driven 32-agent Redis fuzzing campaign - both cloning source and chaining exploits at machine cadence, 'separable only by whether somebody said yes beforehand'. reasoning_so_that names the detection keys explicitly ('machine-authored-payload volume, LLM-style artifacts, and agent-loop telemetry'), and those three keys demonstrably cannot separate authorized research from intrusion. The trace needs an authorization/consent dimension it currently lacks. Second, smaller reframe on reasoning_landing: validation.5ac08c68bc5c5700 (2026-07-25) records that the name arrived roughly nine days after the intrusion and came from the operator's own internal correlation rather than from any threat-intelligence process, which cuts against 'two-plus threat-intel vendors or a MITRE ATT&CK technique' being the mechanism that does the naming. Nothing here contradicts the prediction; the argument needs to absorb what a category would actually have to key on.

Verdict covers all ten bridges. The set is the healthiest in this batch: dimensions split sensibly across because/given/so_that, scores track the actual strength of each day's evidence, and validation.311d29b934381fc3 (2026-07-15, rel=2, dim='none') is an honest negative that says plainly 'Nothing today involves a machine acting as the attacker' rather than manufacturing support. No text-versus-score mismatch of the kind found on validation.5b732ffe3f54c82f, and no misfiled paragraph of the kind found on validation.09f880fb970069a4. The relevance_drift that gated this prediction (2 through 2026-07-20, 4 from 2026-07-21) is a real evidence step - the Hugging Face attribution - not scoring noise.

judgements.reason: reasoning_given ('Chinese labs keep shipping frontier-adjacent open weights around US compute-export limits') is now materially incomplete. Today's report carries New York Times reporting of 2026-07-25 that the administration's working preference is targeted restrictions on SPECIFIC NAMED Chinese open-weight models rather than a categorical ban, with Kimi K3 - this prediction's named vehicle - the model named, assembled from sanctions, procurement pressure and soft signalling rather than any single readable instrument. That is a different constraint class from compute-export limits, and it lands precisely where this prediction's outcome is MEASURED: an aggregate capability index scores models through served access. Same-day sibling prediction.fd7bdbc998adaac2 forecasts exactly that the restriction bites at the serving and procurement layer and not at downloads - weights stay fetchable while US-served access narrows - which is a pathway that could keep an open-weight model off the outright top of the Artificial Analysis Index with no capability gap at all. Rewrite must also re-check reasoning_landing, whose trigger 'after K3 weights drop' is scheduled for 2026-07-27, i.e. tomorrow.

Verdict covers all five rows, which are sound and unusually restrained about what did and did not get measured - validation.04463baa76474c66 and validation.6b96737693dadc65 both state plainly that no Artificial Analysis Index result was published, and validation.6f4d67ab8a6b7dc3 (2026-07-23) records that by Moonshot's own account K3 still trails Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol. So the gap is prediction-specific rather than a quiet news day, and it covers the three days running up to this prediction's own named trigger.

Covers the whole three-actor Need-set (open-weight lab training team, Chinese-lab compute procurement, rival GLM/Qwen lab).
